content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price increases (e.g., 80+ → 60s), then corrects downward — model lags in recognizing mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the 2nd half of the forecast horizon, particularly after day 15–20.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the true mean reversion speed — prices return to mid-range faster than model suggests.
- Model overreacts to recent low prices, pushing forecasts too low when true price rebounds.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — e.g., 80 → 60 → 62.5, model predicts 60 → 55 → 58, missing the rebound.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- Model is overly optimistic in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–5) — tends to predict higher prices than true outcome, then corrects.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shifts — e.g., post-2024-02-01, prices stabilize around 55–65, model doesn’t reflect this plateau.
